verdict.line: You lose this lane if you right-click Jax through his Counter Strike or grind a trade past three exchanges into his Relentless Assault ramp; you win it by poking with Q/W/E and timing your all-in for the window right after his E goes down.

brief.thesis: Jax's whole trade pattern is built around E (Counter Strike), which dodges all incoming basic attacks and then stuns anyone still swinging on him when it ends — but Ornn almost never trades with basic attacks anyway, since Volcanic Rupture, Bellows Breath, and Searing Charge are all ability damage that stance can't dodge. The 51.9% win rate over 1038 games reflects that structural fit: Ornn is naturally suited to fight around Jax's defining tool rather than through it, even though Jax's faster-cooling Leap Strike (17s down to 5s) and zero-cooldown R give him the edge in a straight all-in, which is exactly why OP.GG flags Jax as the solo-kill favorite despite the lane being even on paper.

theirWindow.when: Jax has Q, W, E all up
theirWindow.what: He leaps in with an Empowered strike, then holds Counter Strike to dodge your return damage and stun you when it drops. Don't auto-trade here — back off and make him waste the stance on nothing, or poke with Q/W instead of right-clicking.

yourWindow.when: right after Jax burns his E
yourWindow.what: Counter Strike is 18/16/14/12/10s depending on rank, so once he's used it to dodge poke or clear a wave, it's down for a long stretch. Slow with Q (Volcanic Rupture), charge E (Searing Charge) into a wall for the knockup, and finish with W (Bellows Breath) for Brittle — free autos with no stun risk.

start.why: Jax's early damage is single-target auto and Empower strikes — the Shield's block-and-regen proc directly answers that poke pattern better than raw HP, and it's run in 40% of games at 51.8% WR.

boots.why: Jax's R (Relentless Assault) and W (Empower) are both basic-attack scaling tools with no cooldown on the ultimate — flat damage reduction from autos is the correct answer, and it's the 73.7%-pick, 51.4%-WR standard.

core.why: HP and armor with a burn passive that punishes him for standing in melee range during extended skirmishes.
Jax's entire kit funnels through basic attacks — Thornmail turns every Empowered strike and R proc against him, part of the 64.8%-WR path.
Stacking resistances closes out the build path that hits 64.8% WR over 54 games and makes you nearly unkillable by level 13+.

runes.keystoneWhy: Counter Strike's long early cooldown (18s at rank 1) means pre-6 lane is attrition through short pokes, not one big trade — Grasp sustains you through that and permanently grows the HP pool you need for the level 6+ all-in.

summoners.why: The 72.1%-pick, 51.3%-WR standard — Teleport resets you to lane after poke exchanges instead of forcing an extended auto-trade into his E, and lets you answer his Leap Strike disengages on plates.

playing.title: Poke, don't auto-trade
playing.detail: Lean on Q (Volcanic Rupture) and W (Bellows Breath) instead of extended basic attacks. Counter Strike dodges all incoming basic attacks and stuns you if you're still swinging when it ends — right-clicking into his stance is how Ornn players lose the solo-kill stat despite the even overall win rate.

playing.title: Punish early Leap Strike cooldowns
playing.detail: Jax's Q is 17s at rank 1, falling to just 5s by rank 5. Early levels, meet a landed leap with your own E (Searing Charge) toward terrain so the shockwave knocks him up before his kit resets.

playing.title: Time all-ins around his dead E
playing.detail: Counter Strike runs 18/16/14/12/10s by rank. Once he's burned it on a creep or to dodge your Q, Q-slow into E-charge into W-Brittle lands free damage with zero stun risk.

playing.title: End fights before his R ramps
playing.detail: Relentless Assault has no cooldown and gives stacking attack speed with bonus damage every third hit, so skirmishes that drag past 4-5 exchanges start scaling in his favor. Close it fast or close it with your own R.

playing.title: Double-apply Brittle with R
playing.detail: Call of the Forge God's elemental applies Brittle on first contact — recast to charge into it and redirect for a second knockup and a second Brittle stack. Landing both before he can Counter Strike is how Ornn wins the all-in despite Jax's raw solo-kill edge.

playing.title: Buy Thornmail on curve
playing.detail: Jax's whole kit is auto-attack scaling, so Thornmail from the 64.8%-WR Sunfire Aegis > Thornmail > Jak'Sho path punishes every strike he throws — build it second regardless of who's ahead.

playing.title: Don't fish Q through minions
playing.detail: Volcanic Rupture is only 800 range and needs a clean line to the fissure's end point. Jax's 700-range Leap Strike closes that gap in one cast, so throw Q as he commits to the leap, not before, or the slow whiffs.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, boots, and summoner picks above are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1) — the win rates and pick rates are real. The tactical reading — trade patterns, cooldown windows, and the power-curve calls — is my own analysis layered on top of the live ability text.
